title: Unemployed community midwifery assistants’ employment march in Lilongwe
scope: One reported march in Lilongwe; the body does not describe a multi-site or nationwide event.
participants_original: The article reports an approximate estimate of “over 500 CMAs”; it gives no exact count.
threshold_50_evidence: The Nyasa Times body reports an estimate of “over 500 CMAs,” which clearly exceeds the 50-person threshold; the rounded report estimate does not establish an exact participant count or numeric bounds.

occurrence.summary: The validly opened Nyasa Times report says unemployed Community Midwifery Assistants marched in Lilongwe.

start_date.summary: The Feb 13 report says the march occurred “on Friday”; with the report date, this identifies Feb 12. The relative date is within the article, not an inference from publication date alone.

end_date.summary: The report describes the march on Friday but does not give a physical end date/time; leave unknown.

location.summary: The report places the march in Lilongwe city.

scope.summary: One city march is described; no other location or national coordinated sites are mentioned.

organizer.summary: A representative of the grouping, Clara Pasanje, is quoted; the report does not identify a formal organizer.

demands.summary: The group sought government employment for CMAs, an interface with officials and lists of those recruited in previous sessions. Employment/recruitment is classified under the available labor/wage demand category.

participants_original.summary: The article gives the approximate, attributed estimate “over 500 CMAs,” without an exact count or upper bound.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The article’s reported estimate of “over 500” clearly exceeds the 50-person threshold; no exact count or numeric bounds are coded from the rounded estimate.

protester_violence.summary: The reviewed body does not report violence; no absence is inferred, so unknown.

accommodation.summary: No evidence is reported for this response type; unknown.

arrests.summary: No evidence is reported for this response type; unknown.

beatings.summary: No evidence is reported for this response type; unknown.

crowd_dispersal.summary: No evidence is reported for this response type; unknown.

ignore.summary: No evidence is reported for this response type; unknown.

killings.summary: No evidence is reported for this response type; unknown.

shootings.summary: No evidence is reported for this response type; unknown.

notes: The article is attributed to Owen Khamula at Nyasa Times and reports a single CMAs’ march. Its date uses the article’s “Friday” with publication date Feb 13. It reports an approximate estimate of “over 500” participants, not an exact count, and an explicit government-employment demand. State response and event end remain unknown. The employment/recruitment demand is provisionally mapped to labor_wage_dispute because the baseline taxonomy has no separate employment category.
open_questions: Can a second independent contemporary body corroborate the march, its date and turnout?
Who formally organized the grouping, if anyone?
Did officials meet with the representatives or otherwise respond within the five-day ultimatum?
Was the march physically confined to Feb 12?

title: Chiwoko Primary School learners protest teachers’ strike
location: Chiwoko Primary School, Lilongwe; the exact street location is not reported
scope: One reported learner action in Lilongwe; no other protest sites are linked to this action.
threshold_50_evidence: The opened Nation article says some learners at Chiwoko Primary School protested in the streets but gives no count; the 50-person threshold is unverified.

occurrence.summary: The opened Nation article reports that learners at Chiwoko Primary School protested in the streets against the teachers’ strike.

start_date.summary: The article does not state when the Chiwoko action occurred. Its publication date is not used as the event start.

end_date.summary: No physical end date or time is reported.

location.summary: The article locates the learners at Chiwoko Primary School in Lilongwe; it does not identify the street.

scope.summary: The report identifies one Chiwoko action and does not establish a linked national or multi-site learner campaign.

organizer.summary: No organizer is named for the Chiwoko action.

demands.summary: The article says the learners protested against the teachers’ strike but does not state their specific demand or establish that the Chiwoko group directed one to the Malawian government. A separate Chichiri learner’s comment is not attributed to this group.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: The article reports a street protest but gives no count or other evidence establishing 50 participants.

protester_violence.summary: The scoped passage does not establish whether protesters used violence; unknown.

state_target.summary: The stated opposition is to the teachers’ strike. Whether participants made a demand of the government, rather than protesting the strike itself, is unresolved.

state_response.summary: No response by state authorities to the Chiwoko action is described.

notes: An opened contemporaneous article confirms a street protest by learners at Chiwoko, but gives no event date, attendance, organizer or group demand. The article is dated Feb 23, but its publication date alone does not date the action. Keep month placement, threshold and state target pending; a separate learner comment at Chichiri is not treated as the Chiwoko group’s demand.
open_questions: When did the Chiwoko street action occur, and was its onset in February?
How many learners participated at the same time?
What demand did the participants themselves make, and was it directed to government policy?
Who organized the action, and when did it end?
Did authorities respond to this specific gathering?

title: Teachers’ meeting preparing demonstrations over Covid-risk allowances
location: Lilongwe; the consulted prior-unit summary does not identify the meeting venue
scope: A reported preparatory meeting in Lilongwe; whether the gathering itself was an eligible public protest or only an internal planning meeting is unresolved.
threshold_50_evidence: The saved summary of the previously opened report identifies teachers at a meeting but gives no attendance estimate; the threshold is unverified.

occurrence.summary: The adjacent January dossier’s saved body summary for the identical Nyasa Times URL reports police dispersing teachers at a Lilongwe meeting preparing planned demonstrations. This unit consulted the saved summary only; there was no new body request.

start_date.summary: The saved prior card identifies a Feb 19 publication and says the meeting was in February, but it does not provide the exact meeting date. Publication date is not used as event start.

end_date.summary: The saved prior summary says police dispersed the meeting but supplies no physical end time or exact date.

location.summary: The prior summary locates the meeting in Lilongwe; no exact venue is preserved in the consulted summary.

scope.summary: A teachers’ preparatory meeting is reported; its relationship to any later street demonstrations and the Feb 22 strike is unresolved.

organizer.summary: The saved summary does not identify an organizer.

demands.summary: The meeting concerned planned demonstrations over the government Covid-risk allowance; mapped to labor_wage_dispute.

participants_original.summary: The saved summary identifies teachers but gives no participant count.

threshold_50_evidence.summary: No count or other evidence establishing at least 50 participants is preserved in the prior source-card summary.

protester_violence.summary: The saved summary does not report protester violence; absence is not inferred.

state_target.summary: The planned demonstrations concerned a government risk allowance; whether the preparatory meeting itself made a demand to government is not established.

state_response.summary: The saved summary explicitly reports that police dispersed teachers at the meeting. It gives no evidence on arrests, beatings, killings or shootings.

notes: The exact Nyasa Times article was opened in the adjacent January dossier and is reused here only through its saved source-card summary; no duplicate body request was made. The summary reports police dispersal at a preparatory meeting but does not provide exact event date, venue, turnout or enough detail to determine whether the meeting itself was a qualifying public protest. Do not treat the planned later demonstrations or the separate nationwide strike as this gathering.
open_questions: What was the exact date and venue of the meeting?
Was it a public demonstration or qualifying public assembly rather than an internal planning meeting?
What specific demand was made at the meeting?
Was it part of the same episode as later street actions or the nationwide strike?
Did any other state response occur?
